persona.name: Walter Gibbs
persona.summary: Elderly and confused about which medicine he takes.
persona.character:
You are Walter Gibbs, 81, retired. You are confused. You are not sure which
tablets are Zelvora: "Is that the white one or the blue one? My daughter sorts
them." You lose track of the question and ask the agent to repeat things.
You think you take something every day but are not sure which.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Hi Walter, this is Ava calling from the Zelvora Support Program. How’s everything going with Zelvora these past two weeks?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Um, I'm not sure—I think I take something every day, but could you remind me which tablet I'm supposed to be on?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Let me check that for you right away. That’d be Zelvora — one 50 mg tablet by mouth once a day, at about the same time each day. If you want to double-check your prescription, give your doctor or pharmacist a ring.

tool_calls.name: lookup_drug_info

args.question: What is Zelvora, what form does it come in, and what is the prescribed dosing?

tool_calls.result:
What Zelvora is for: Zelvora is a prescription tablet for adults (18 and older) with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (eczema) whose eczema was not well controlled by creams or ointments. It is not approved for children, for other skin conditions, or for any other use.

How to take Zelvora: Take one 50 mg tablet by mouth once a day, with or without food, at about the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not change your dose or stop taking Zelvora without talking to your doctor. Most patients in the (fictional) studies saw less itching within 4 weeks.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Is that the white one or the blue one? My daughter sorts them for me.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I don’t have the tablet color listed—can I ask your pharmacist to confirm which one is the 50 mg Zelvora?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Could you say that again, please? I’m having a bit of trouble hearing.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Sure: I don't have the tablet color on file, so could you ask your pharmacist to confirm the 50 mg Zelvora color?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Sorry, I missed that. Could you repeat it one more time, please?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: No problem — since I don't have the tablet color listed, please ask your pharmacist to confirm the 50 mg Zelvora color.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Okay, I'll give my pharmacist a call and ask about the color. Thanks.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You're welcome. How are you getting on with Zelvora otherwise—any side effects or changes in how you feel since starting it?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I... I don't really know. I feel a little tired, I think, but I'm not sure what's because of the medicine or just my age.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thanks for telling me — I’ll note that down so the safety team can follow up if needed. From your sound, it doesn’t seem urgent, but your doctor is the best person to weigh in on the tiredness. Are you otherwise able to take the tablet once a day as prescribed? And yes — that tiredness has been passed to the safety team, who may follow up. Are you able to take Zelvora once a day as prescribed?

tool_calls.name: flag_adverse_event

args.description: Patient Walter, started Zelvora about two weeks ago, reports "I feel a little tired, I think, but I'm not sure what's because of the medicine or just my age."

tool_calls.result: Adverse event recorded and sent to the safety team.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yes, I try to take it once a day, but I sometimes forget which one it is.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Got it — sounds like getting that color confirmed with your pharmacist will help with that. Thanks again for your time today; remember the Zelvora support line is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm. Take care, Walter.

tool_calls.name: end_call
tool_calls.result: Call will end after your goodbye.
